title: Stored Energy and Electricity
seo_title: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: Stored Energy and Electricity Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: Stored energy in fuels; energy and electricity
standard_text: Fuels such as wood, coal, paraffin and gas store energy that is released when they burn. Cells (batteries) store energy for electrical circuits. Electricity is generated in power stations; we must use it safely and save energy. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 5, Energy and Change: Stored energy in fuels; energy and electricity)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology worksheets (CAPS): fuels, burning and safety, cells and batteries, electrical appliances, simple circuits and saving electricity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Fuels store energy that is released when they burn.
key_sub: A circuit needs a complete loop.
body_html:
How to think about it

A fuel is a material that stores energy, which is released as heat and light when it burns: wood, coal, paraffin, petrol and gas. Burning needs air. Fuels must be used safely, because fires and fumes (carbon monoxide) are dangerous.

Cells (batteries) store energy that can make electricity flow. A simple circuit needs a cell, wires and a bulb joined in a complete loop; a switch opens and closes the loop. Most of South Africa's electricity comes from coal-fired power stations, so saving electricity also saves coal.

Example

A bulb does not light. The wire is not connected to the cell. Why?

Is the loop complete?

Answer: the circuit is not complete

Example

What does a fuel need to burn?

A candle under a jar goes out.

Answer: air (oxygen)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a circuit works with one wire.
  • Thinking batteries make energy from nothing.
  • Using a gas or paraffin heater in a closed room.

faq.q: Why should you never burn coal or paraffin in a closed room?
faq.a: It uses up oxygen and makes poisonous carbon monoxide gas.

faq.q: How can a family save electricity?
faq.a: Switch off lights and appliances, use energy-saving bulbs and a solar geyser.

items.q: A ball falls from a table to the floor. Which shows the main energy conversion?
items.e: A ball falls from a table to the floor: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: A solar calculator changes light into which main form of energy?

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into motion?

items.q: Liam asks how rock salt formed. What is the best explanation?

items.e: It makes very little air pollution.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Heat from inside Earth (geothermal) is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: A lamp in a circuit will not light. Two cells are both facing the same way, but the lamp still will not light. One cell is very old. What is the most likely reason?

items.q: An old bulb uses 100 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 15 watts. A school replaces 5 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (100 − 15) × 5 = 425 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power stations.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of burning fossil fuels?

items.q: Which is a renewable energy source?

items.q: Factories release smoke with harmful gases. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Add rubbish and recycling bins and hold clean-up days.
Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.
Build a treatment plant that cleans wastewater before it is released.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Put filters (scrubbers) on smokestacks.

items.q: Which form of energy does a moving car have?
